title: Vegan Nachos Supreme
subtitle: with Lentils, Salsa Fresca and 'Sour Cream'
description: It’s plant power all the way with our super-tasty vegan dishes! Our meat-free, dairy-free, honey-free dishes are amped with plant-based proteins, fresh produce, nuts and seeds. Best of all, they’re for everyone, whether you’re vegan, vegetarian or flexitarian.

steps.text: Cook lentils: Check your avocado is ripe before starting this recipe (see Cooking tip). Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Add the lentils, then reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 22-25 mins until the lentils are tender. Drain the lentils, then wipe the pan clean and reserve.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Finely chop the onion. Halve the tomatoes. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. To make the salsa, put half the onion, half the tomatoes and 2 tsp red wine vinegar in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Soften veggies: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the reserved pan over medium-high heat. Cook the remaining onion and remaining tomatoes, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the garlic and Tex-Mex seasoning and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant.

Simmer veggies: Add the lentils, tomato paste, 1½ tbs barbecue sauce and 2 tbs water to the veggie mixture in the pan and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 mins until slightly thickened. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Bake chips and serve up: Meanwhile, put the corn chips on an oven tray and bake for 5 mins. Cut the avocado into thin wedges. Divide the corn chips, lentil mixture, salsa, avocado and vegan sour cream among plates. Or, pop everything on the table for everyone to help themselves. Enjoy!
Make it herby: If you have some on hand, scatter over a handful of coriander or parsley leaves for a burst of freshness. Or, coarsely chop them and stir through the salsa.
